what_it_does: When designing a processor, engineers must choose among thousands of micro-architecture settings (pipeline depth, cache sizes, number of execution units, etc.) while trying to balance multiple goals like speed, power, and area all at once — a problem called design-space exploration. Traditional automated search algorithms work blindly, ignoring the accumulated wisdom of human experts. LEMOE uses a large language model (LLM) to inject expert knowledge into a mathematical search technique called Bayesian optimization (which builds a probabilistic model of which designs are likely to be good, then samples smartly). The LLM first suggests a set of promising starting-point designs using its knowledge of chip architecture, giving the optimizer a head start rather than random guesses. The same LLM is then used to improve the internal prediction model when only sparse data is available, because it can reason about why certain configurations might be good even before many real measurements exist.
